mlag.note: Two independent Nexus switches form a vPC domain for active/active multichassis link aggregation, over a peer link built from front-panel Ethernet ports. Each peer keeps its own control and management plane; this is not a stack

stacking.note: No hardware stacking. Nexus switches are deployed as independent systems; multichassis redundancy is vPC

routing.summary: NX-OS Layer 3: static, OSPFv2/v3, IS-IS, EIGRP, RIPv2, BGP/MP-BGP, PIM-SM/SSM, MSDP, HSRP, VRRP, VXLAN BGP EVPN, Segment Routing. Layer 3 unicast and multicast routing require a license beyond the default Layer 2 feature set

licensing: Default system software covers Layer 2 security and management. Layer 3 unicast and multicast routing and Nexus Data Broker need additional licensing; sold as Data Center Networking (DCN) Essentials, Advantage or Premier subscriptions, or perpetual
routeScale: Hardware forwarding tables are shared; the platform is published as up to 40 MB shared buffer with flexible LPM and host scale. Per-model route scale is in the Cisco Verified Scalability Guide, not the data sheet
macTable: Not published per model on the data sheet; see the Cisco Verified Scalability Guide
macsec: Not listed on the N9200 data sheet

power.summary: Two hot-swappable power supplies (1+1) and hot-swappable fan trays, in port-side intake or port-side exhaust airflow versions. AC, DC and HVAC/HVDC options vary by model

note: Platform total is up to 7.2 Tbps and 5.35 bpps across the family. Native line-rate VXLAN routing is supported on every model except the 92348GC-X and 92348GC-FX3. N9K-C92160YC-X (end of sale, last order Mar 5, 2021) is intentionally excluded
verifyNote: Route and MAC scale are not published per model on the N9200 data sheet; they need the Verified Scalability Guide. Lifecycle: only the 92160YC-X was confirmed end of sale. The 9272Q, 92304QC and 9236C are the same generation and their lifecycle status was not confirmed

models.note: 1G ToR and out-of-band management switch. No native line-rate VXLAN routing
